methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements, and ensuring that each statement focused on a single, well-defined aspect of the system's functionality or design.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The system consists of a one-dimensional array of 512 cells (q[511:0])
Each cell can be either on (1) or off (0)
The state of the entire system advances by one time step on each clock cycle
The next state of each cell q[i] depends on its current state and the states of its two neighbors, q[i-1] and q[i+1], according to the Rule 110 table
Boundary cells q[0] and q[511] should consider their non-existent neighbors q[-1] and q[512] to be off (0)
A synchronous active-high load input allows initializing the state of the system
When the load input is asserted, the state of the system is loaded with the data provided on the data[511:0] input
spec_atomic_units: Module implements a 512-cell Rule 110 cellular automaton
Module has input clk
Module has input load
Module has input data[511:0]
Module has output reg [511:0] q
Output q updates on the rising edge of clk
When load is high, q is updated with the value of data on the rising edge of clk
When load is low, q is updated with the next state of the cellular automaton, calculated based on the current state of q and the Rule 110 logic, on the rising edge of clk
The next state of q depends on the current state of q and the combinational logic implementing Rule 110
The critical path is from q through the Rule 110 combinational logic back to q
The setup time for data with respect to clk when load is asserted must be met
The setup time for the signals that determine the next state of q with respect to clk when load is deasserted must also be met
Implements Rule 110 update rule for each cell
Boundary conditions are handled by treating q[-1] and q[512] as always being zero
Combinational logic consists of 512 identical circuits
Each circuit takes three inputs (the cell itself and its two neighbors) and produces one output (the next state of the cell)
The load signal is not part of the combinational logic for the next state calculation
The combinational logic calculates the next state of each cell based on its current state and the states of its neighbors
The Rule 110 update rule is defined by the provided truth table
The leftmost cell (q[0]) uses a fixed value of 0 for its left neighbor (q[-1])
The rightmost cell (q[511]) uses a fixed value of 0 for its right neighbor (q[512])
